prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Regional Dispatch Center (Juniper), 24/7 regional EMS dispatch; zones have primary/alternate routes to Emergency Department (ED) and Riverside Trauma Center. Center creates incident record, preserves caller report, escalates readiness gaps, produces Unit Staging Change Card, records authorization time, unit-selection reason and routes, maintains coverage picture, and keeps controlled procedures for record review, system changes and corrective actions. It uses Battery Swap Voucher, North Approach Queue Snapshot and Caller Location Correction Slip. Modes: Surge (entered at queue-age, high-priority-call or staffing thresholds; Center declares level). Degraded radio: emergency traffic prioritized; network operators announce outages; crews acknowledge on fallback channels and repeat location/destination; if voice fails, dispatchers shall use the approved data channel and log every contact attempt; after restoration they shall reconcile delayed reports against timestamps and preserve discrepancies. Mutual aid when objectives are missed. Shift handover: outgoing shift records incidents, failures, temporary channels and pending decisions; incoming shift verifies assignments and paths before accepting control; Shift Commander keeps authority until a named successor acknowledges. Actors: Call Taker Mara (Larkspur): produces Caller Location Correction Slip, receives Bedside Arrival Receipt, keeps caller connected. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield): sets priority, flags calls needing immediate radio, sends Pediatric Acuity Note, approves overrides, reviews Duplicate Incident Audit Memo. Regional Medical Director: clinical policy and advice. Dispatcher: recommends units. Shift Commander (Sundial): approves exceptions, sends Mutual Aid Release Form, receives Coverage Gap Bulletin, adjusts staffing. Radio Coordinator (Mistral): uses Regional Radio Network and Unit Staging Change Card, logs channel changes, sends Coverage Gap Bulletin. Paramedic Crew: reports status; avoids unconfirmed areas. Hospital Liaison Desk (Kestrel): confirms capacity, by phone if disrupted; produces Bedside Arrival Receipt. ED gets backup arrival updates. Fleet Maintenance Cell (Bluejay): produces Battery Swap Voucher, reports vehicle and radio faults. Data Quality Officer (Pebble): sends Duplicate Incident Audit Memo, checks timestamps, samples records. Systems: Computer Aided Dispatch Console (shows status with time and source). Ambulance Coordination Platform (queues updates, flags reconciliation). North Gate Status Board and South Gate Status Board (access conditions). Ambulance Unit 417 reports position and status on reconnect.

New part:
S224: The Triage Supervisor reviews cases in which acuity decisions or escalation timing may have affected patient risk.
S225: The Regional Medical Director reviews clinical findings and approves changes to clinical guidance within the scope of regional authority.
S226: Audit findings identify the records examined, the criteria applied, and any limitations that affect interpretation.
S227: The Regional Dispatch Center retains audit evidence under approved access and retention controls.
S228: The Fleet Maintenance Cell uses the Mutual Aid Release Form to support accountable maintenance and availability records.
S229: Material findings are assigned to a responsible role with a due date and a documented method for verifying closure.
S230: The Shift Commander may restrict an operational capability when an unresolved defect creates unacceptable risk.
S231: The Regional Dispatch Center records the rationale, scope, and duration of each such restriction.
S232: Changes to the Ambulance Coordination Platform are assessed for operational, clinical, security, and continuity impacts before release.
S233: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console is tested against approved scenarios before a change is authorized for regional use.
S234: Release approval records identify the change owner, test evidence, known limitations, and rollback approach.
S235: The Radio Coordinator uses the South Access Lane Notice as part of accountable operational review.
S236: The Regional Radio Network and its interfaces are checked after maintenance or configuration changes before normal use resumes.
S237: Fleet Maintenance Cell schedules preventive work according to manufacturer guidance, service history, and regional operating requirements.
S238: Maintenance records include the asset identifier, work performed, parts used, and return-to-service decision.
S239: The Ambulance Coordination Platform is monitored for availability, response time, data integrity, and interface failures.
S240: The Regional Dispatch Center reviews service measures at a defined cadence and compares results with approved operating thresholds.
S241: Performance reviews consider demand, coverage, dispatch delay, communications availability, and unresolved data quality issues.
S242: The Hospital Liaison Desk contributes relevant operational observations while protecting information that is not required for the review.
S243: The Regional Medical Director and Shift Commander review significant events that may indicate a need for clinical or operational improvement.
S244: Corrective actions are tracked through verification so that completion is distinguished from demonstrated effectiveness.
S245: Recurring issues are evaluated for systemic causes rather than closed solely through local workarounds.
S246: Approved lessons are incorporated into procedures, training, maintenance plans, or release criteria as appropriate.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
